terms.comment: The adjective used as a noun; plural chēmica, chemicals.

terms.gloss: a drug, a prepared substance: medicine, poison, dye
evidence: Plin. NH 27.101: medicāmentō sagittās tingere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The classical word nearest to “a chemical”: any prepared substance that acts on a thing, as a remedy, a poison or a dye (Lewis & Short). Its usual sense is a medicine (see medicine); use it for a chemical only where the context shows it.

chemicum.html: Greek χημεία, with eta; Morgan–Owens s.v. chemistry writes chêmicus. See chemical (adjective).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 165, 290. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. chemical, chemistry.
Lewis & Short has no entry for chemicum.
